full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah J: This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 21-3-2002 passed by the learned District Judge, Lakshmipur in Family Appeal No. 3 of 2000 affirming with modification the judgment and decree dated 31-1-2000 passed by the learned Family Court Judge and Assistant Judge, Ramgonj, Lakshmipur in Family Suit No. 21 of 1996. 

 2. Shahinoor Akhter @ Bijlee, wife of the defendant as plaintiff, instituted a Family Suit No. 21 of 1996 in the Family Court Ramgonj, Lakshmipur against the defendant-petitioner Ikhtiar Hossain Choudhury praying for decree claiming Taka 5,81,501 in total on account of dower, maintenance for herself and for her sons Younus Arafat and other miscellaneous claims as detailed out in the schedule to the plaint. 

 7. The learned Family Court Judge and Assistant Judge by its judgment dated 31-1-2000 decreed the suit in part on contest allowing Taka 75,000 as dower money, Taka 66053 as maintenance and Taka 57,600 on account of maintenance of Younus Arafat. 

 8. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree, the defendant preferred Family Appeal No. 3 of 2000 in the Court of the District Judge, Lakshmipur who heard the appeal and passed the impugned judgment and decree on 21-3-2002 affirming the judgment and decree of the Family Court Judge with some modification. 

 9. It is against the aforesaid judgment and decree passed by the District Judge, the defendant-appellant moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 10. Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that Younus Arafat, the son of the petitioner and the opposite party, was born on 30-11-1986; that he attained the age of puberty on 31-11-2000 and that the learned District Judge, committed an error of law resulting in an error in his decision occasioning failure of justice in decreeing that the defendant-petitioner is bound to give maintenance allowance to Younus Arafat even after his attainment of puberty and till completion of his education, which is not sacramental. He further submits that this sort of decree of the learned District Judge runs counter to the recognised principle of Mussalnzan's personal law. He further submits that learned District Judge also resorted to arithmetic in calculating amount of decretal money and his judgment has resulted in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 45. It is definite case of the plaintiff-opposite party with the exception of the months of September and October, 1994 the defendant-petitioner did not maintain her and son Yunus Arafat from May, 1988 to the date of divorce 8-2-1995. This case has been brought home to us in view of the overwhelming evidence on the side of the plaintiff-opposite party and from the discussions made hereinbefore. Be that as it may, the Family Suit No. 21 of 1996 was instituted in the Family Court concerned on 10-7-1996. A reference to the impugned judgment shows that the learned Family Court Judge has awarded monthly maintenance allowance Taka 800 to the plaintiff Shahinoor Akhter @ Biglee and monthly maintenance allowance of Taka 600 to the son Yunus Arafat in the absence of any stipulation in that behalf in the relevant column of the kabinnama (Exhibit 1). The learned appellate Court also accepted this monthly allowance rate which -decided by the trial Court. Under the circumstances made above, monthly rates shown by the trial Court as well as appellate Court may be adopted by this Court for the purpose of fixation of the maintenance allowance of the plaintiff-opposite party and her son. In view of the above discussion and legal position Shahinoor Akhter @ Bijlee is entitled to get past maintenance for 4 years 7 months from 10-7-1990 to 10-7-1996 plus 3 months for Iddat period that is 4 years 10 months at the rate of Taka 800 per month which stands at Taka 46,400. The maintenance for 2(two) months of Taka 1600 will be deducted from Taka 46,400 and consequently, the net amount of maintenance stands at Taka 44,800 as against Taka 58,666 decreed by the appellate Court. Her son Yunus Arafat will get past maintenance for 6 years from 10-7-1990 to 10-7-1996 and also will get maintenance from date of birth on 30-11-1986 to the attainment of puberty on 30-11-2001 and thus the total period of maintenance stands at 11 years and 5 months and the amount of maintenance of this period at the rate of Taka 600 per month stands at Taka 82,200. The maintenance of 2 months at Taka 1200 (when he resided with his father) will be deducted from 82,200 and thus the amount stands at Taka 81,000 as against Taka 83,222 which was decreed by the Court of appeal below. So, it is seen that in all Shahinoor Akhter and Yunus Arafat together will get Taka 44,800 + 81,000 = 1,25,800 from the defendant-petitioner Ikhtiar Hossain Choudhury. 

 46. It appears from record that as per Court's order dated 12-4-2003, the defendant-petitioner deposited Taka 60,000 which was received by Shahenoor Akhter @ Bijlee and her son Yunus Arafat which will be deducted from Taka 1,25,800 and now they, in all, will be entitled to get Taka 65,800 (sixty-five thousand and eight hundred) only from the defendant-petitioner Ikhtiar Hossain Choudhury. Since the learned Appellate Court has failed to consider some vital decisions and also misinterpreted the principles of authoritative decisions in the matter of fixation of age, for getting maintenance period of past maintenance and period of Iddat and further miscalculated the amount thereof. So, the judgment and decree of the appellate Court is liable to be modified with above observations.
